etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English tresorie, from Old French tresorie, from tresor (“treasure”), from Latin thēsaurus (“treasure”), from Ancient Greek θησαυρός (thēsaurós, “treasure house”). Displaced native Old English māþmhūs.

definitions.definition: A place where treasure is stored safely.
A place where state or royal money and valuables are stored.
A collection of artistic or literary works.

quote.citation: 1599, W. Kinsayder or Theriomastix [pseudonyms; John Marston], “Totum in Toto”, in The Scourge of Villanie. […], London:  […]  I[ames] R[oberts], →OCLC; republished as G[eorge] B[agshawe] Harrison, editor, The Scourge of Villanie (The Bodley Head Quartos; 13), London: John Lane, The Bodley Head […]; New York, N.Y.: E[dward] P[ayson] Dutton & Company, 1925, →OCLC, page 56:
quote.text: Now since he hath the grace, thus gracelesse be / His neighbors sweare he'le swell with treasurie.
